memories.author: patient
memories.text: Intake note: Follows a Jain diet, so avoids onion, garlic, potato and other root vegetables. Does not eat after sunset. Every year she fasts for the 8 days of Paryushana (August to September), taking only boiled water during the day.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: TSH 6.8 mIU/L (reference 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L). HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin) 6.1 % (reference below 5.7 %; prediabetes 5.7 to 6.4 %).

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o hypothyroidism on levothyroxine (Thyronorm) 50 mcg OD. C/o tiredness and dry skin, weight up 2 kg in 6 months. Jain diet as noted. Takes tablet on waking, mostly on empty stomach.
O: BP 124/80 mmHg, pulse 70/min, ht 160 cm, wt 63 kg. Thyroid not palpably enlarged. TSH 6.8 mIU/L. HbA1c 6.1 %.
A: 1. Hypothyroidism, under-replaced (TSH 6.8). 2. Prediabetes, HbA1c 6.1 %, no glucose-lowering medicine indicated.
P: 1. Continue levothyroxine 50 mcg OD; repeat TSH in 3 months before any dose change. 2. Regular walks. 3. Recheck HbA1c at next review.
Adv: Include millets, dal and fibre at meals; regular walking; keep tablet on empty stomach. R/V in 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: TSH 7.9 mIU/L (reference 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: Tired, feels cold, constipated at times. Currently observing the Paryushana fast (boiled water during the day). Levothyroxine taken most mornings, sometimes after tea.
O: BP 126/82 mmHg, pulse 68/min, wt 64 kg. TSH 7.9 mIU/L, up from 6.8.
A: 1. Hypothyroidism, not controlled on 50 mcg OD.
P: 1. Increase levothyroxine (Thyronorm) to 75 mcg OD. 2. Take on waking with water, 30 to 60 min before tea or food. 3. Repeat TSH in 3 months.
Adv: Tablet with plain water only, not with tea or milk. Continue walks as the fast allows. R/V in 3 months.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Rx change: levothyroxine (Thyronorm) increased from 50 mcg OD to 75 mcg OD. Once daily on an empty stomach, from 2025-08-19.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: TSH 3.2 mIU/L (reference 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: Energy better, bowels regular now. Taking the 75 mcg tablet on an empty stomach. Jain diet, no root vegetables; eats millets 2 to 3 times a week.
O: BP 122/78 mmHg, pulse 70/min, wt 62 kg. TSH 3.2 mIU/L, now within range.
A: 1. Hypothyroidism, controlled on levothyroxine 75 mcg OD.
P: 1. Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg OD. 2. Repeat TSH in 6 months.
Adv: Continue tablet on empty stomach, 30 min before food. Walk 30 min daily. R/V in 6 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: TSH 2.6 mIU/L (reference 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L). HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin) 6.0 % (reference below 5.7 %; prediabetes 5.7 to 6.4 %). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: Feels well on levothyroxine, tiredness and constipation resolved. Jain diet continues. Asks what she should eat to keep her blood sugar in check.
O: BP 120/76 mmHg, pulse 68/min, wt 61 kg. TSH 2.6 mIU/L. HbA1c 6.0 %, stable from 6.1 %.
A: 1. Hypothyroidism, euthyroid on levothyroxine 75 mcg OD. 2. Prediabetes, HbA1c 6.0 %, not on any glucose-lowering medicine.
P: 1. Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg OD. 2. Prediabetes diet plan: 3 meals plus 2 small snacks a day, including millets (ragi, jowar, bajra) at one meal. 3. Avoid sweets and sweetened drinks. 4. Walk 30 minutes daily. 5. Recheck HbA1c in 6 months.
Adv: 3 meals and 2 small snacks a day; include millets; no sweets; walk 30 min daily. R/V in 5 months.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Routine thyroid follow-up with Dr Anjali Mehta (D01) booked for 2026-10-12 at 10:30. Please bring the levothyroxine strip and any notes on tiredness or bowel habit. Take the morning tablet as usual; no fasting is needed for the appointment itself.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient: 'Doctor, Paryushana starts next week and I plan to observe the 8-day fast again, with boiled water during the day and no eating after sunset. Should I change the timing of my thyroid tablet during the fast? Kindly advise. Thank you.'
